chunks.heading: Am I Me Enough
chunks.notes: The speaker recasts young love as a test of self-worth ("wasn't that always the question... am I real enough for this love") and catalogs triadic images of self-sanding to seem worthy.

chunks.heading: Am I Me Enough
chunks.notes: Triadic "mistook... mistook... mistook" catalogs the chase for external permission, closing on the direct rhetorical question of self-worth.

chunks.heading: Am I Me Enough
chunks.notes: "So was I good enough? Maybe that was the wrong question" pivots into anaphoric affirmations marking a turn toward self-recognition.

chunks.heading: Am I Me Enough
chunks.notes: The three-line close ("I finally learned I was enough because I was mine") delivers the poem's explicit aphoristic answer to its own title question.
